URL: https://www.lse.co.uk/news/uk-markets-position-for-burnham-premiership-yields-tick-up-sterling-strengthens-v0iyjjgk5r631pn.html
NOTE: Reuters (via LSE, 20 Jul) — Gilt yields rose and sterling dipped as investors feared looser fiscal policy after Burnham's "flexibility" remarks. 10-year gilt yield +8bps to 5.04%; 30-year +9bps to 5.75% (highest in two months). Sterling last -0.17% at $1.3429, flat vs euro at 85.04p. British yields already highest in G7; 10-year hit 18-year high in May amid Iran war energy costs. Liz Truss mini-budget scars weigh on bonds. Neil Wilson (Saxo Markets): "the market has shown some emerging signs of nervousness about the mood music... Mood music so far is the lurch to the left [is what] markets were worried about – big spending vibes."
